correctness.rationale: Exact Cauchy projection representation reduces four facet vectors to seven axes. The classical pseudo-face square-sum identity excludes three or four maximal singleton axes; the equality equations force an exhaustive rank-three area-vector family. Minkowski existence yields genuine tetrahedra. For t=1/2 the exact ten-center Gram matrix gives maximum mutual inner product 3/4, and the two shorter candidate axes have norm 1/sqrt(2); hence ten disjoint caps yield the sharp terminal tail on z>=sqrt(7/8). The included executable independently checks symbolic norms, rank and Gram contact, numerical Cauchy/subset equality, and two simulation points. Finite checks are supplemental only.

value.rationale: The maximum number of brightest viewing axes is a natural shape invariant for spatial tetrahedra. Using a previously known pseudo-face identity, the result improves the obvious combinatorial upper bound of seven to a sharp geometric five, determines the entire nonsymmetric equality locus, and turns its symmetric member into an exact rare-extreme shadow law with a sharp first-overlap threshold. These jointly constitute a complete meaningful extremal classification rather than a routine reparametrization or isolated constant.
